explanation: Catfish carry taste buds over their whiskers, fins and skin as well as in their mouths, so they can taste food in murky water before they reach it.

claims.text: A channel catfish has more than 100,000 taste buds.
An adult human has up to about 10,000 taste buds.
Catfish have taste buds on their barbels (whiskers), fins and skin as well as in the mouth.
Catfish can taste food in the water before reaching it.

writerNotes: Self-check (guide 9.3), all eleven codes confirmed true. The selfCheck field itself is left out because the CNT-1 item schema refuses it as an unknown key, so the codes are recorded here. lint: content:check reports no errors and no warnings for this item. claims: four listed; high: c1 (number, a comparison label) and c2 (number, a comparison label); standard: c3 and c4. datasets: no pinned dataset in content/datasets/manifest.json covers animal or plant biology (it holds countries, languages, currencies, cities, elements, Nobel Prizes, Olympic Games, World Cups, art collections and Natural Earth), so none applies, and the high-risk claims need web evidence from checker A; one search on catfish and human taste bud counts should cover c1 to c3. rivalTest: Argued for the human, the obvious pick, which is why counterintuitive is set. Both values are bounds: sources put channel catfish at well over 100,000 (often around 175,000) and adults at 2,000 to 10,000, so the catfish wins by at least ten times under any figure on offer. volatility: evergreen, a settled fact that cannot change; no time words, and nothing rests on knowledge newer than mid-2026. regional: catfish are farmed and eaten on every inhabited continent. style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, explanation of 28 words. myths: screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. mystery and encore: nothing of either kind in a comparison item. doubts: none on the order of magnitude; the bounds are written so that differing counts never flip the answer.

evidence.restatement: A channel catfish has well over 100,000 taste buds spread over its body; estimates I know run to about 175,000 or more.

issues.note: c1 'more than 100,000' is a high-risk number I could not confirm; common figures run from about 100,000 to 175,000 and some sources say less. Use a bound that every source clears (for example 'tens of thousands', against about 10,000 for a person) or confirm the figure externally. The answer is unaffected.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: I couldn't find the 175,000 figure in these results. The closest number is a lower estimate. A ScienceDirect overview says catfish, which locate food almost entirely by taste, have numerous taste buds (over 100,000) scattered all over their skin. That source is a general reference page and doesn't name Caprio as the origin of the count.

claimResults.note: Three searches (12 to 14, Tier A and B sites only, among them the US Fish and Wildlife Service, the Missouri Department of Conservation, the National Park Service and PubMed) found no count for the channel catfish. The only figure, 'over 100,000', is for catfish in general, from one reference page, so the species-specific number stays uncertain. The direction of the comparison is not in doubt: the agency pages say taste buds cover the whole body.

issues.note: The label value 'more than 100,000' for a channel catfish has no species-specific source. Find one, or restate the label for catfish in general with the reference figure, or use a bound that has its own evidence (pass B's fix). The answer is unaffected; the changed claim needs fresh checks.
